_comment: The block manifest consumed by `klt signoff --manifest` (klayout-tools
issue #722, Phase 0 of epic #706). This is the file the fleet tier
roll-up (2AMLogic/2am#956) consumes to grade this block's T1 state
mechanically, replacing the hand-maintained checkbox list on issue #3
-- see the `## The verdict of record` section there and issue #155 for
the contract.
block             required. Identifies this block's row in the fleet
roll-up, which consumes exactly this value.
kind              required. `mixed-signal`, confirmed against this
block rather than taken from issue #155: the TRNG
partitions into an analog entropy source plus
digitizer bank (design/sampler_core.spice's
`.subckt sampler_core`, laid out as
layout/sampler_core/sampler_core.gds) and a
digital conditioner/health section
(digital/rtl/trng_digital.v, synthesized in
digital/flow/). The partition boundary is stated
explicitly on issue #3 and in signoff/README.md;
the mixed-signal claim makes both columns of the
per-kind items (1, 2, 5, 7, 11) apply, once per
partition.
evidence          item id -> evidence entry. Partition-qualified
keys (`<id>.<analog|digital>`, klayout-tools
signoff's _lookup_evidence prefers them) are used
deliberately: a kind-independent item is graded
only for the partition whose evidence actually
backs it, so `3.analog` does not paint a `met` on
the digital partition: `3.digital`/`4.digital` cite the
separate layout/trng_digital/ envelopes (issue #211).
Cited for the digital partition (issue #211, 2026-10-09; the P&R macro
layout/trng_digital/ delivered by #166):
3.digital          layout/trng_digital/drc.json: `klt drc` status clean,
0 violations, curated sky130 deck, pinned to
provenance.input.content_hash (sha256 of the committed
trng_digital.gds). Curated-deck limits are disclosed in
signoff/README.md from the envelope's coverage block
(not foundry DRC; rule-free layers and skipped rules).
4.digital          layout/trng_digital/lvs.json: status match, engine
klayout, power_connectivity.status `match`, vs the
signal-pin-only routed gate-level Verilog; pinned to
provenance.input.content_hash (sha256 of the extracted
trng_digital.layout.abstract.spice it compared).
Signal-pin-only reference and warnings-only
topology.* mismatches are disclosed in
signoff/README.md; body_verification is `unchecked`.
11.digital         (issue #223) [layout/trng_digital/erc.json, pnr.json,
lvs.json]: native `klt erc --findings-only` on the
committed routed trng_digital.gds with
layout/trng_digital/erc-supply-spec.json (generated by
erc-gen-supply-spec.py from the GDS + pnr.json): VPWR
and VGND each one island, zero findings, stackup
covers every pnr.json strap layer (met1/met4/met5) and
every DEF special-net layer (met1..met5), the drawn-nwell
tie (43 wells / 704 tapcells) and a 704-box substrate
tie are both in erc_coverage.checked with nothing
skipped. erc is pinned to provenance.input.content_hash
(the committed GDS sha); pnr.json is pinned to its
recorded input (the synthesized netlist sha); lvs.json to
its netlist sha as for 4.digital. Disclosures
(substrate tie is a caller-asserted-box well assertion,
antenna half not run, negative controls) are in
layout/trng_digital/ERC.md and signoff/README.md.
What is deliberately NOT cited, item by item, against the current
tree (2026-10-09, @ origin/main):
1, 2, 9, 10       no klt verb backs these (klt signoff grades them on
'some passing envelope was cited', not topical
relevance); citing an unrelated passing envelope to
make the row go green is exactly what this manifest
exists to prevent. They render unmet/no_evidence.
5.analog           no `klt sim` envelope exists -- sim/ campaigns are
minted evidence records (sim/bin/evidence_record.py
shape), not `klt sim` output.
5.digital           layout/trng_digital/sta.json exists (16 Liberty
corners, all constrained, non-negative setup/hold,
SPEF-annotated) and the pinned 0.7.0 grader would
render the row `met` on it alone. It is deliberately
NOT cited: item 5's digital rule is multi-corner STA
PLUS a bit-exact functional suite recorded as
evidence, and no `klt functional-verification`
envelope exists. Citing the STA half alone would
paint a green row for half the rule (and the spec
ratification caveat). Update (issue #222): native
`klt functional-verification` reports now exist
(sim/digital-functional-verification/records/20261009-120511-d9f51a4),
functional/unit-delay, RTL and routed netlist. They
are still NOT cited: item 5's own note requires a
ratified spec and DR-0004 (digital section) is
`Proposed`. Stays unmet/no_evidence.
6                  no `klt yield` report exists.
7.analog           no `klt pex` report exists -- post-layout
campaigns run from `klt extract --parasitics`
netlists via sim/bin harnesses, which item 7 by
design does not accept (a clean DRC or
pre-layout sim proves nothing post-layout).
7.digital          (issue #227) CITED: a native, SDF-annotated `klt
functional-verification` report
(sim/digital-sdf-timed-verification/runs/20261009-172301-8cbd26a/timed-declared.report.json):
environment.sdf.annotated true, 13/13 tests, routed
netlist vs the independent oracle. Disclosures that
travel with it: sdf.partial is true (Icarus 13.0
drops all 455 TIMINGCHECK sections, so setup/hold are
NOT simulated, and 33 zero-delay alias-port
INTERCONNECT entries); 39 zero-delay
bit-selected-input-source INTERCONNECT entries were
removed before annotation (Icarus cannot resolve
them); a SINGLE SDF corner (tt_025C_1v80), not a PVT
sweep; wire delay is zero in the SDF; DR-0004 is
`Proposed`, so the verdict is provisional. Negative
controls (mistargeted SDF, removed SDF, exact
+137 ps arc shift, +15000 ns shift, 5 ns clock) are in
the same record. The 16-corner STA (item 5) is not
replaced. Item 5.digital is unaffected and stays
unmet/no_evidence. Cited UNPINNED: a pin renders
`unverifiable_provenance` because the
functional-verification envelope records no input
hash, so freshness is as strong as regenerating the
record when the netlist or SDF changes (the
record's input-hashes.json pins every input).
8                  no aggregated, current characterization artifact
exists yet; a hand-rolled `"kind": "generic"`
wrapper asserting status pass would be a
self-attestation, not evidence.
11                 the item-11 `klt erc` supply evidence exists AND is
now cited (issue #161): `erc-supply-spec.json`
declares `ties[]` for every distinct well/substrate
tie this block draws -- 70 merged nwell regions to
vdd, 5 each to vddr1..vddr4, and the substrate to vss
-- graded `erc_status: clean` with zero findings and
a non-empty `erc_coverage.checked` (all six ties,
also listed in `checked_by_well_assertion`: the
per-supply well regions are asserted boxes derived
from the drawn nwell, because 0.6.0 checks every
merged polygon of a whole drawn well layer against
one net and this block's wells tie to five different
supplies) and nothing in `skipped` (sky130's tap is a
dedicated layer, so no tie is degenerate). The erc
citation is pinned to the envelope's
provenance.input.content_hash -- the committed
GDS's sha, same pin value as item 3; the SPEC's own
hash rides in the envelope's
provenance.spec.content_hash. The row still renders
`unmet`, for a reason that is now the LVS half
alone: `lvs_supply_unproven`. The grader's
no-PDN branch requires every declared supply to
appear in the cited lvs.json's
net_correspondence as a row whose ENTIRE
layout-side string equals that supply name -- but
klt lvs joins a label-merged net's aliases with
'|', so this block's six supply rows read
'G_VDDR_M1|...|VDDR|VDDR1' etc. and can never
equal 'vddr1' (no single-name supply row exists:
checked, 0 of 152). No spec-side name fixes both
halves at once (the ERC half needs real label
names; the LVS half needs exact alias-string
equality), so the citation is filed as the honest
mechanical verdict and the alias-joined-rows
pairing gap is filed upstream (friction protocol;
see signoff/README.md's item-11 section for the
issue link and the local follow-up). The
The digital column is cited separately as
11.digital (issue #223); see above.
Freshness pinning (`content_hash`): pinned wherever the cited
envelope's own shape records one. `layout/sampler_core/drc.json`
records provenance.input.content_hash, so item 3 is pinned to it;
that value is sha256 of the committed sampler_core.gds, so a
regenerated DRC against a changed GDS no longer matches the pin and
renders the item stale -- the manifest rots loudly, not silently.
Issue #181 regenerated sampler_core (sky130-fixed cut sizes, licon
cuts on the 0.005 um grid) and moved the GDS pin from a00f6550... to
e3ff54a9...; drc.json and erc.json were both re-run against the new
GDS, not just re-pinned. The same regeneration rewrote
`layout/sampler_core/lvs.json` on a klt build whose envelope records
provenance.input.content_hash (the sha256 of the extracted
sampler_core.spice it compared, role `netlist`), so item 4 and
item 11's lvs half are now pinned too -- before #181 the 0.4.0
envelope carried no input hash and item 4 was file-backed with no
pin. The LVS pin is the netlist's hash, not the GDS's: the GDS ->
netlist link is extract.json's own provenance.input.content_hash
(the GDS pin above).
Regenerate the committed report (signoff/t1-report.json) with the
exact command in signoff/README.md -- the report embeds the
--tiers-doc label verbatim, so the invocation must match byte for
byte. CI re-runs the same command and diffs, so this file cannot
cite a changed artifact without going red (issue #155, `CI re-runs
it`).
